notable_absence.finding: Unlike DDL statement pages in this same batch (ALTER BUCKET, ALTER GROUP, ALTER USER), the cbq page names no capella-role gate at all. Its own access model is a third, narrower shape: single administrative username/password credentials that cannot be switched mid-session ('This option requires administration credentials and you cannot switch the credentials during a session.'). This is neither the management-plane capella-role gate nor the Basic/Advanced data-plane privilege pair - it's a client-tool-level credential constraint that sits alongside both.

cross_component_finding: cbq's own client version ('SHELL VERSION : 7.6.2-3721', 'GO VERSION : go1.22.2') is a genuine, discrete version number for a downloadable command-line tool package - this is legitimately different from the known anomaly where Capella *service* pages cite server/-style version strings despite Capella itself having no discrete version. The page is careful to distinguish the two: 'Use N1QL queries select version(); or select min_version(); to display server version' (i.e., the query engine's version, separate from the shell's own version) - so cbq.md correctly keeps 'shell version' and 'server version' conceptually distinct, even while both are literal version strings.
